applies_why: The judge text uses verses (Matthew 1:18, 25, and Luke 1:34) to break a link, which is exactly the act the rule's last sentence governs.
quote: CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union
rule_words: counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.
room: The phrase 'A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way': either it means such a verse counts only under the just-stated conditions (the judge must quote the earlier-round sentence that pressed it against the link and name that round), or it means such a verse counts toward breaking a link without those conditions; I weighed the first reading because 'this way' points back to the conditions just stated, and the second reading would leave the sentence with nothing to do.
why: The judge broke C3's link with Matthew 1:18, 25 (and Luke 1:34) while quoting only scripture, never the sentence of an earlier round that pressed these verses against that link, and naming no round (the rounds-named line is empty), so under K-G4 these verses do not count and the link-break stands on verses the rule disqualifies.
